intro.eyebrow: Kids allowance as a family partnership
intro.title: Pocket Money Calculator
intro.body: Parent and child set a short background, answer together, and get a family allowance plan: a fair monthly range, spend/save/give split, and practical tips. Everything stays in the browser.

profiles.talk-first: Talk first — then set the amount

insights.dim-moneyResponsibility-high: There’s real ownership of money — keep a simple tracker so it doesn’t fade.
insights.dim-moneyResponsibility-low: When cash “vanishes” without a story — write what happens when the wallet is empty.
insights.dim-savingDiscipline-high: Saving feels real — celebrate small milestones out loud.
insights.dim-savingDiscipline-low: Without a visible goal, saving slips. Put a goal photo by the jar.
insights.dim-familyPartnership-high: Partnership feels present — renew the rules every few months.
insights.dim-familyPartnership-low: If only one side decides, allowance becomes a fight. Take 15 minutes to co-write rules.
insights.dim-spendingWisdom-high: There’s a pause before buying — reward that muscle with words, not only money.
insights.dim-spendingWisdom-low: Impulse asks break budgets. Try a 24-hour rule for non-urgent wants.
insights.overall-strong: The base is strong — write down amount, split, and empty-wallet rules.
insights.overall-steady: Good direction with a few soft spots — pick one habit for the next two weeks.
insights.overall-developing: Willingness is there, rules are fuzzy. Simplify before raising the amount.
insights.overall-needs-care: Reset gently: smaller amount, clearer rules, conversation without blame.
insights.age-young: At this age, visuals win — colorful jars and counting coins in hand.
insights.age-tween: Friend pressure rises — practice a polite “not this week” and plan ahead.
insights.age-teen: Digital independence needs transparency without smothering surveillance.
insights.model-fixed: With a fixed model: match the amount to responsibility — not only convenience.
insights.model-chores: With chores: separate family duties from paid extras — don’t trade dignity for cash.
insights.model-hybrid: Hybrid works best with a stable base plus a clear bonus lane for saving/enterprise.
insights.goal-delay: For delayed gratification: a waiting rule matters more than a bigger sum.
insights.goal-save-goal: For a big goal: break it into short milestones with dates.
insights.goal-independence: For independence: allow a small mistake — then review it together.
insights.goal-value: For money value: compare prices and keep a small give share in the split.

tips.tip-sunday-reset: Sunday reset: count what’s left and sketch the week in two minutes.
tips.tip-empty-wallet-plan: Write the empty-wallet plan — no automatic parent bailout.
tips.tip-visible-tracker: A visible tracker (notebook/simple app) — 30 seconds after each purchase.
tips.tip-pay-yourself-first: On payday: move savings first, then fun money.
tips.tip-photo-goal: Goal photo on the fridge or lock screen — daily reminder.
tips.tip-match-small: A small parent match on savings (e.g. 1:1 up to a cap) motivates without buying everything.
tips.tip-family-meeting: A 15-minute monthly allowance meeting — amount, what worked, what changes.
tips.tip-chore-menu: Chore menu: family duties vs paid bonus tasks — written and clear.
tips.tip-two-voices: Rule changes need both voices — child and parent.
tips.tip-24h-pause: Non-urgent buys above an agreed threshold wait 24 hours.
tips.tip-needs-wants-list: One-page needs vs wants list — refresh weekly.
tips.tip-give-jar: A small give jar: pick a cause together each quarter.
tips.tip-monthly-review: Month-end: what we learned, not only what remained.

habits.habit-jar-split: Three jars/envelopes: spend, save, give — at the agreed percentages.
habits.habit-receipt-photo: Snap a receipt or jot it down immediately — memory rewrites stories.
habits.habit-goal-countdown: Countdown to the goal: weeks left and weekly shortfall.
habits.habit-praise-ritual: Praise good process — not only cool purchases.
habits.habit-no-bailout-default: Default: no automatic bailout. Exceptions only after an agreed talk.
habits.habit-earn-bonus-lane: A capped bonus lane for small enterprise/extra tasks — without replacing the base.

money-runs-out.prompt: When money runs out before the period ends — we have a clear plan (no drama).

byAge.young: When the coins run out early — we know what happens without big tears or anger.
byAge.tween: When allowance ends mid-way — there’s a clear rule instead of a fight.
byAge.teen: When the budget ends early — we agree what happens (no automatic loan).

track-what-spent.prompt: We roughly know where most of the money went lately.

byAge.young: We remember/draw where the coins went.
byAge.tween: There’s a simple tracker — notebook or note — for what we bought.
byAge.teen: There’s light tracking (app/note) without surveillance vibes.

ask-before-borrow.prompt: Borrowing from parents/siblings only happens after a clear ask — not “just because”.

own-mistakes.prompt: When a purchase was a mistake — we talk honestly without shame spirals.

byAge.young: If we regret a buy — we say it out loud and move on.
byAge.tween: Buying mistakes are lessons, not punishments.
byAge.teen: We review a bad purchase together — without a long lecture.

plan-the-month.prompt: At the start of the period we have a rough idea how money will split.

no-secret-spending.prompt: No secret spending that breaks trust at home.

save-before-spend.prompt: Some money goes to savings before the fun spending starts.

goal-feels-real.prompt: There’s a savings goal that feels real to both sides.

byAge.young: There’s a visible goal (photo/toy) we’re moving toward.
byAge.tween: There’s a clear goal with a rough date.
byAge.teen: There’s a priced goal and a weekly plan.

wait-for-want.prompt: We can wait a bit before a non-urgent purchase.

byAge.young: Sometimes we say “let’s think tomorrow” instead of buying now.
byAge.tween: There’s a waiting rule for non-urgent wants.
byAge.teen: There’s a conscious pause before impulse buys (online/friends).

celebrate-milestones.prompt: We celebrate saving progress — not only the final purchase.

protect-savings-jar.prompt: Savings are protected — not “borrowed from” without agreement.

byModel.fixed: Even with a fixed amount — savings don’t get swallowed by daily spend.
byModel.chores: Chore bonuses don’t replace the savings jar.
byModel.hybrid: In the hybrid path it’s clear which share is locked for saving.

match-encourage.prompt: Saving gets positive encouragement (words or a small match) — not only pressure.

byModel.fixed: Even on a fixed model we encourage saving without buying everything for the child.
byModel.chores: Paying for chores doesn’t cancel the value of saving.
byModel.hybrid: There’s a clear encouragement lane for saving/enterprise.

chores-vs-pay.prompt: We’re clear what is a family duty vs a paid task.

byModel.fixed: Even without paying for every chore — expectations as household partners are clear.
byModel.chores: There’s a transparent chore list and rates — no daily haggling.
byModel.hybrid: There’s a stable base plus defined bonus tasks.

rules-were-agreed.prompt: Allowance rules were agreed together — not just announced.

both-voices-heard.prompt: Both parent and child feel heard in money talks.

byAge.young: The child helps choose jars and the goal.
byAge.tween: Both sides get a say before changing rules.
byAge.teen: There’s an adult dialogue — not a one-way lecture.

review-together.prompt: We occasionally check if the amount and rules still fit.

fair-when-busy.prompt: Even in a busy week — agreements hold without silent punishment.

byModel.fixed: The amount arrives on time as agreed.
byModel.chores: Fairly canceled chores don’t become vague money punishment.
byModel.hybrid: The base stays stable even when there’s no bonus that week.

praise-not-only-pay.prompt: Good money habits get praise in words — not only cash.

sibling-or-friends-pressure.prompt: We talk honestly about friend/sibling pressure around buying.

byAge.young: We explain why we don’t buy everything a friend has.
byAge.tween: We practice answers to social pressure about money.
byAge.teen: There’s an open talk about status, brands, and real budgets.

impulse-pause.prompt: Before a spontaneous purchase there’s a pause.

byAge.young: Sometimes the want goes on a “tomorrow list”.
byAge.tween: There’s a waiting rule for non-urgent things.

needs-vs-wants.prompt: We can tell needs from wants without shaming the feeling.

give-back-share.prompt: There’s a small place for giving/donation in the split.

compare-prices.prompt: Sometimes we check an alternative price before buying.

byAge.tween: We check if a reasonable alternative exists.
byAge.teen: We compare prices/deals before a relatively big buy.

digital-vs-cash.prompt: We understand digital money also “runs out” — not only coins.

byAge.young: We talk about cards/apps being real money too.
byAge.tween: There’s a clear limit for digital spend if it exists.
byAge.teen: There’s basic transparency on digital spend without month-long audits.

earn-extra-ok.prompt: There’s a fair way to earn a bit more — without turning home into a marketplace.

byModel.fixed: Small enterprise outside the fixed amount is ok when coordinated.
byModel.chores: Bonus chores are defined ahead — not endless haggling.
byModel.hybrid: The enterprise/bonus lane is clear and capped.
